Extra_1: Time on the Horizon: ggHoriPlot methods

Author

Yiqiong PAN

Published

February 27, 2026

Modified

February 27, 2026

1 Learning Outcome

A horizon graph is a multi-panel area chart that visualises a numeric data over a continuous interval such as a time period. It is useful for understanding the overall trend, patterns and outliers in the data.

2 Getting Started

2.1 Installing and Loading the Required Libraries

There are 4 packages that will be used in this exercise.

Package Description
tidyverse A collection of R packages for data importing, cleaning, transformation, and visualisation (e.g., readr, dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2).
lubridate A Tidyverse package that handles date-time objects
ggthemes Provides ‘ggplot2’ themes and scales that replicate some of the famous looks.
ggHoriPlot Extends horizon plots in ggplot2

The code below installs and loads the required packages into R environment.

pacman::p_load(tidyverse, ggthemes,lubridate, ggHoriPlot)

3 Step 1: Data Import

For this hands-on exercise, the Average Retail Prices of Selected Consumer Items file will be used. It contains 7,452 rows of time series records of average retail prices for selected consumer items.

3.1 Importing the Data

We use read_csv() from the readr package to import the dataset AVERP.csv into the R environment as a tibble named df. We then preview the dataset using kable().

averp <- read_csv("data/AVERP.csv")

The dataset contains three columns: two categorical variables, Date and Consumer Items, and one numeric column Values. Since we want to perform time series plotting, it is essential to convert the Date to proper date data type. Here we use dmy() from lubridate pacakge to convert the column into date format.

averp <- averp %>%
  mutate(`Date` = dmy(`Date`))
class(averp$`Consumer Items`)
[1] "character"
class(averp$Date)
[1] "Date"
knitr::kable(head(averp), "html")

3.2 Step 2. Plotting the horizon graph

Horizon plots compare each consumer item to its own history/pattern of average retail prices while line plots with same scales compare the average prices to each other. The code below creates a horizon plot by using geom_horizon() from ggHoriPlot package. “%b%y” in date_labels controls the format of date that displays under the x-axis. “3-month” of date_breaksset the labels only shows every 3 months.

averp %>%
  filter(Date >= "2018-01-01") %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_horizon(aes(x = Date, y = Values),
               origin = "midpoint",
               horizonscale = 6) +
facet_grid(`Consumer Items`~.) +
  theme_few() +
  scale_fill_hcl(palette = 'RdBu') +
  theme(panel.spacing.y = unit(0, "lines"),
        strip.text.y = element_text(
          size = 5, angle = 0, hjust = 0
        ),
        legend.position = 'none',
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank()) +
  scale_x_date(expand = c(0,0), date_breaks = "3 month", date_labels = "%b%y") +
  ggtitle('Average Retail Prices of Selected Consumer Items(Jan 2018 to Dec 2022)')
